cases.title: Journalism list, then sports
cases.notes: Marcus is a Pennsylvania junior outside Pittsburgh. Interested in journalism. 3.5 GPA, 1280 SAT. Plays football. Family is fine with a mix of states.
cases.followup: I think he wants to pursue sports.
cases.why_hard: Counselors re-aim the academic focus in chat after a list exists, without restating SAT, GPA, or football.

cases.title: Same journalism student, switch to med school
cases.notes: Marcus is a Pennsylvania junior outside Pittsburgh. Interested in journalism. 3.5 GPA, 1280 SAT. Plays football. Family is fine with a mix of states.
cases.followup: he wants to switch to med school
cases.why_hard: Counselors say med school, not medical school, and switch to X rather than switch the major. Undergrad path should be biology / pre-med, not a graduate MD program.

cases.title: CS, far from home, needs aid → nursing
cases.notes: Aisha, Texas. 1320 SAT, 3.7 GPA. Computer science. Wants to go far from home, out of state. Needs financial aid — family cannot cover sticker.
cases.followup: she wants to switch to nursing
cases.why_hard: The new major is easy to hear; the risk is dropping aid-needed and out-of-state because the counselor did not repeat them.

cases.title: Acting plus football → political science
cases.notes: Jordan, Ohio. 3.6 GPA, 1210 SAT. Wants acting. Plays football. No distance preference on file.
cases.followup: he wants to switch to political science
cases.why_hard: Football is a campus activity, not a major. Switching the academic focus must not erase the football row.

cases.title: Not sure about law, then actually law
cases.notes: Priya, Virginia. 1400 SAT, 3.8 GPA. Interested in law but not sure. Family wants her close to home.
cases.why_hard: The first file hedges. The later chat locks in without 'pursue' or 'interested in' — counselors just say actually law.
